description:
Give the event-log parser one torn-line rule: ignore a final line without a terminating newline and reject any other malformed line.

## Background

`domain::parse_known_events` (`crates/jit/src/domain/event_log.rs:42-80`) skips a malformed line only when the next line is a profile-lifecycle record whose `isolated_torn_tail` is true (`certifies_preceding_torn_tail`, `:78`). Event appends now land at the committed length, so an unterminated final line is an uncommitted append that never becomes a middle line. The parser's tests are at `event_log.rs:96-160`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `parse_known_events` ignores a final line that has no terminating newline, skips blank lines and records with a retired tag, and returns an error naming the line for any other line that is not a well-formed event record.
- [hard] REQ-02: No reader certifies a malformed line by the record that follows it, and `certifies_preceding_torn_tail` no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-03: One parser unit test owns the rule: an unterminated final line is ignored, and a malformed middle line is rejected.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Event-log readers ignore an unterminated final line
